_what: How much each thinker moved the argument, 0 to 100. This is an editorial judgement, not a measurement, and it is kept in its own file so it can be read and argued with rather than buried in code.
_why_not_measured: The obvious measure is the shape of the graph itself -- who is read by how many later people. Run on this corpus it puts Aristotle first, Heidegger second and Plato sixth, because the edges cover the twentieth century far more densely than antiquity. It records how the book was written, not how the field went.

_scale.90-100: the field is unimaginable without them; everyone after is arguing with them
_scale.75-89: founded a position the argument still runs on; unavoidable in any survey
_scale.55-74: substantial: shaped a school, or a debate that outlived them
_scale.38-54: important inside a tradition or a century
_scale.25-37: the long tail: real contributors, read mostly by people who study the period
